items.title: Coachella Sues Walmart for Selling Knockoffs at Stores Near Festival: ‘Who Needs the Merch Tent?’
items.summary:
Coachella is suing Walmart over accusations that the retail giant has sold fake festival merchandise for years despite repeated demands to stop.

In a lawsuit Tuesday (Nov. 24), the owners of the festival accuse Walmart of infringing Coachella’s trademarks by plastering the name and logo on shirts, tumblers and other items, often at stores located near the Empire Polo Club grounds where the yearly festival takes place.

Related

Coachella’s attorneys, representing the AEG unit Goldenvoice that runs the festival, say they’ve been asking Walmart to stop since as far back as 2017 to no avail, leaving the festival “with no option but to bring the present lawsuit.”

“Plaintiffs have made repeated requests and demands for Walmart to cease selling and advertising infringing goods,” Coachella’s lawyers write. “Plaintiffs’ requests have been of minimal benefit; Walmart typically stops for a period of time, but then resumes.”

The case claims Walmart is targeting festivalgoers at nearby stores, citing knockoff merch at locations in La Quinta, Calif., and North Indio, Calif., both of which are a short drive away. It cites the La Quinta Walmart selling coolers and folding chairs under a direct copy of the festival’s logo, as well as an in-store display featuring a miniature version of the Ferris wheel…

items.title: The Chicks & Willie Colón Join AI Music Lawsuit Against Suno: ‘Misappropriated Identities’
items.summary:
The Chicks , Willie Colón and Sam Moore are joining the legal fight against AI music.

The trio of acts and their estates were among a slew of artists added Tuesday (Nov. 24) to a case filed this summer against Suno, accusing the AI song generator of breaking the law by allowing users to “conjure up a beloved musician’s identity” when they enter a name as a prompt.

Related 

Suno, Anthropic Face $1B Copyright Lawsuits From Round Hill Music Over AI Training 

Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support — For Now — to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight 

Rod Wave Indicted on Drug & Gun Charges for Items Allegedly Found in Car After Speeding Stop 

The case, filed by Jason Isbell , was a novel action centered on artists’ likeness rights, unlike earlier lawsuits over AI labs using copyrighted music to train models. Now, that case is backed by the star power of a huge country trio, a Latin music titan and an R&B legend.

“Suno built and trained a model to index musicians by name,” lawyers for the artists write. “It encoded musicians’ identities into its AI model to create its commercial product without consent, and now exploits those identities by publicly using musicians’ names to Suno’s considerable commercial benefit.”

In addition to the members of the Chicks (Natalie Maines, Martie Maguire and Emily Strayer) and the estates of the late Colón and Moore, the lawsuit was also joined by 10 more artists, including David Longstreth of the indie rock band Dirty Projectors;  Carl Craig, a pioneering DJ of Detroit techno; Franz Nicolay of rock band The Hold Steady; and Kealiʻi…

items.title: Andy Burnham says UK government have “negotiated language that may make it easier in future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”
items.summary:
Andy Burnham has addressed the issues facing artists across the UK, and said that the government has “negotiated language that may make it easier in future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”.

READ MORE: UK touring bands are suffering due to “Brexit fuck-ups and a lack of government control” 

The Prime Minister made the comments in parliament, highlighting the widespread issues facing musicians looking to tour, including rising costs and Brexit – the latter of which putting an end to visa-free travel for UK artists and crew wishing to work and creating an existential threat to the talent pipeline .

Speaking about “touring musicians and artists”, Burnham said that he was “particularly pleased” that his parliament had “negotiated language that may make it easier in the future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”.

Addressing the threats facing the sector, he said that music is “arguably our finest export”, but also “an area we are in danger of taking too much for granted”.

“British music is known and loved around the world. Brexit made it harder to tour, but we now have a chance to explore mutually beneficial solutions,” he added. “We still have work to do, but let me say directly to all our musicians, I fully intend to take this opportunity.”

Burnham’s comments addressing the touring situation for artists following Brexit comes as he attended a major summit in Brussels on Friday (November 20), where the EU and UK announced a new UK–EU “reset” deal that affected food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility…

items.title: ESSENCE Festival of Culture Moving On From New Orleans After Three Decades: ‘Memories Were Made — And So Was History’
items.summary:
After three decades of bringing R&B, funk, hip-hop, soul, blues and zydeco to generations of fans, the ESSENCE Festival of Culture announced on Tuesday (Nov. 24) that it is moving on from New Orleans. In an open letter celebrating 31 years in the Big Easy, Essence thanked the city it has called home since launching in 1995. 

“For more than three decades, you’ve been more than the home of the ESSENCE Festival of Culture. Through every year and every chapter of our annual event, you’ve been part of our family: a destination and community instrumental to our journey, and a culture that has informed and inspired us with every gorgeous sound, unforgettable flavor, and vibrant color,” read the letter.

“Your hospitality has welcomed us. Your traditions have taught us. Every summer, your spirit lifted us,” it continued. “From the sounds of Frankie Beverly & Maze echoing through the Caesars Superdome and the generations who came together in the Ernest N. Morial Convention Center, to the laughter filling the streets, the family-owned restaurants that fed us, and the warm drawl of a ‘bayyy-by,’ every July, you gave our celebration a rhythm that could only belong to New Orleans.”

The farewell noted that the annual gathering had grown into more than just a weekend of music, morphing over the years into a “reunion, a tradition, and a celebration that could only have been shaped by a city like yours. It was a homecoming … It was also a chance to connect with the community: the local artists who shared their gifts, the small business owners who opened their doors, the hospitality…
items.t: ESSENCE Festival of Culture Moving On From New Orleans After Three Decades: ‘Memories Were Made — And So Was History’

items.title: Bonehead to raffle iconic signed Oasis Live ’25 cut-out of himself for charity
items.summary:
Paul “Bonehead” Arthurs is raffling off the life-sized cut-out of himself that Oasis brought out on the Live ‘25 tour , and donating the money to charity.

READ MORE: Oasis live in Cardiff: a supersonic reunion for a new generation 

The cut-out was made after the original and founding guitarist for Oasis was unable to make several shows on the iconic Live ‘25 reunion tour last year as he was undergoing treatment for prostate cancer.

He was given the all-clear from tonsil cancer back in 2022 , but shared early last year that he had been diagnosed with prostate cancer. He then shared an update in October 2025, saying that he would be taking a “planned break” from the shows and sitting out the band’s dates in Asia and Australia so that he could get “the next phase of care”. He later rejoined them for shows in South America towards the end of the year.

In his absence, Noel Gallagher arranged for a life-sized cardboard version of Bonehead to be made to join the group on tour. It was first seen on stage at a show in Goyang Stadium in Seoul , South Korea on October 21, and became a running joke, consistently appearing on stage with the group on various nights and dressed up in different themed outfits.

Now, Bonehead has signed the cut-out and teamed up with The Christie Charity to auction it off for charity. All proceeds will support cancer care and research at The Christie NHS Foundation Trust in Manchester – the hospital that treated him with both his diagnoses.

The sequel to Kahan’s 2024 Live from Fenway Park album features songs recorded at more than a dozen stops on this summer’s tour, including Boston, Atlanta, Chicago, Toronto, San Francisco, Cincinnati, Minneapolis, Los Angeles, Vancouver and Seattle.

items.title: Belle and Sebastian Sign Worldwide Catalog Deal With Matador Records
items.summary:
Matador Records has secured worldwide rights to the complete catalog of Belle and Sebastian , bringing the Glasgow indie-pop group’s recorded output under the independent label’s global representation.

The deal extends a relationship between the band and Matador that dates back to 1998, when the label released the group’s third album, The Boy With The Arab Strap , in North America before subsequently reissuing the band’s 1996 debut Tigermilk .

Under the new agreement, If You’re Feeling Sinister (1996) and The Boy With The Arab Strap , alongside the four EPs collected on 2005’s Push Barman to Open Old Wounds Volume 1 , will be licensed from Bella Figura Music. These titles will carry both the Bella Figura and Matador Records imprints.

Meanwhile, Dear Catastrophe Waitress (2003), The Life Pursuit (2006), Write About Love (2010) and The Third Eye Centre (2013), together with their associated EPs and singles, will be licensed directly from Belle and Sebastian. Originally released under Rough Trade, these titles will be branded as Matador/Rough Trade worldwide. 

The band’s remaining seven albums — Tigermilk , Fold Your Hands Child, You Walk Like A Peasant (2000), Storytelling (2002), Girls In Peacetime Want to Dance (2015), Days Of The Bagnold Summer (2019), A Bit of Previous (2022) and Late Developers (2023) — will be licensed directly from the band and released under the Matador moniker.

The first release under the expanded arrangement will be a 30th anniversary edition of If You’re Feeling Sinister , featuring previously unreleased songs and unheard demos from the era.…
items.t: Belle and Sebastian Sign Worldwide Catalog Deal With Matador Records

items.title: The Beatles’ Apple HQ Experience Set For 2027 – But No Rooftop Concerts Permitted
items.summary:
Here’s another date for your diary, Beatles fans. On Wednesday (Nov. 25), it was announced that plans for a new visitor attraction at 3 Savile Row , expected to open in London in 2027, were approved by Westminster City Council’s Planning Committee.

Dubbed the 3 Savile Row Experience, the attraction will be based inside the Mayfair building that once served as the headquarters of Apple Corps, the company founded in 1963 by Paul McCartney, John Lennon, George Harrison and Ringo Starr to protect their creative and business activity. 

The seven-floor museum is set to house exhibitions, a recreated recording studio, previously unseen archive material delivered with AV technologies and access to the rooftop where the Fab Four played their famous farewell concert and final public appearance on Jan. 30, 1969. The location’s basement was also used as a recording studio for part of the Let It Be sessions. 

The new council permit will not allow live music to be hosted at 3 Savile Row, though there is an option for recorded music. A planned basement cafe and bar will also be allowed to be open to midnight, although capped at 104 events per year to minimize disturbance to the neighbours.

Apple Corps originally left and sold the building in 1976, following The Beatles’ break-up six years prior. The company reacquired the HQ earlier this year, and during a recent visit, Starr described it as “like coming home.”

In a statement, councillor Tim Barnes said: “This is Fab news for fans of the Fab Four, and for Westminster. 3 Savile Row has an extraordinary place in British music history.…
items.t: The Beatles’ Apple HQ Experience Set For 2027 – But No Rooftop Concerts Permitted

items.title: Matthew Perry’s grave headstone ‘Friends’ reference removed
items.summary:
The plaque on Matthew Perry ’s headstone has been updated to remove a reference to Friends .

Matthew Perry was found unresponsive in a hot tub in his Los Angeles home on October 28, 2023. He was later pronounced dead, with his death being attributed to the acute effects of ketamine , and drowning and coronary artery disease listed as other factors.

Earlier this year, Perry’s live-in assistant Kenneth Iwamasa was sentenced to three years and five months in jail after being found guilty of injecting the Friends star with ketamine after working with two doctors to secure $50,000 (£38,000) of the drug in the weeks leading up to his death.

Jasveen Sangha, the drug dealer also known as the ‘Ketamine Queen’, was sentenced to 15 years in prison for supplying the drugs that Perry took before his death while rehab counsellor Erik Fleming, Dr. Salvador Plasencia and Dr. Mark Chavez were also found guilty of supplying Perry with ketamine .

As reported by Entertainment Weekly , a new grave marker was placed on Perry’s grave in January that read: “Matthew Langford Perry. August 19, 1969 – October 28, 2023. Much Loved – Friend –”.

Recently though, that plaque has been replaced. The new headstone still features Perry’s full name but now reads “Rest now. We love you with our whole hearts”.

'Friends' star Matthew Perry's grave marker no longer references his 'Friends' role.

The new plaque at Forest Lawn Hollywood Hills replaces the "Much Loved, Friend" marker, which now reads "Rest Now" followed by "We Love You With Our Whole Hearts."

READ MORE: “It felt like we were changing the world”: inside New Order’s seminal ‘Power, Corruption & Lies’ 

The gig took place on Monday (November 23) as the first date of the band’s 2026 tour of South America, and the first of their two 8,000 capacity shows in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

Kicking off slightly later than usual due to severe weather, the gig was the first full gig since Gillian Gilbert announced that she would not be joining the group on the road due to health reasons. It was also the first full New Order show without drummer Stephen Morris, who has stepped back from international touring.

Morris was the drummer in Joy Division alongside Bernard Sumner , Peter Hook and Ian Curtis , and the remaining members formed New Order with Gilbert after Curtis’ death in 1980. Morris and Gilbert have also released music together outside New Order as The Other Two. Their debut album, ‘The Other Two & You’, arrived in 1993, followed by ‘Super Highways’ in 1999.

In June, New Order confirmed that both Morris and Gilbert would not be touring with them in the “foreseeable future” due to “personal” reasons, and in September, Gilbert told fans that she is living with cancer .

items.title: The Beatles’ new London 3 Savile Row plans approved by council – with “truly immersive experience” planned for rooftop
items.summary:
New plans for The Beatles ’ London 3 Savile Row have been approved by the council, and include a “truly immersive experience” taking place on the rooftop.

READ MORE: Paul McCartney interviewed: “Writing a song is still a magic feeling for me, and hopefully always will be” 

The site was the Apple Corps headquarters in London, and the place where ‘ Let It Be ‘ was recorded. It also was the spot where they played their iconic final public performance in 1969 on the rooftop.

Earlier this year, the company announced it was converting the building into a seven-floor “cultural experience and exhibition” celebrating The Beatles, with a basement café-bar on the site of the studio where they recorded their last album.

It is set to open its doors next year and include seven floors of never-before-seen material from Apple Corps’ extensive archives, rotating exhibitions, a fan store, and a recreation of the original studio where ‘Let it Be’ was recorded. An expected 900 visitors are expected to visit each weekday, and around 1,140 on the weekends – although it was recently confirmed that no live music can be played on the terrace and any amplified music or speech will have to be limited.

Now, it has been confirmed that the plans for 3 Savile Row have been given the seal of approval from the government, and include a “truly immersive experience” that will take place on the rooftop.

The Westminster City Council’s Planning Committee approved the plans last night (Tuesday November 24), confirming that fans will be able to visit the exhibitions, the basement recording studio, and the…
items.t: The Beatles’ new London 3 Savile Row plans approved by council – with “truly immersive experience” planned for rooftop

items.title: ‘Unknown Substance’ Released at Evacuated Don Toliver Show in Manchester ‘Could Be Linked to Jewel Thefts,’ Police Say
items.summary:
Don Toliver ’s disrupted performance at Manchester’s Co-op Live may have been linked to a string of jewel thefts, says local law enforcement.

Related 

Don Toliver’s Manchester Show Evacuated After ‘Unknown Substance’ Released in Crowd 

Don Toliver Delays London Gig After Manchester Set Evacuated for ‘Unknown Substance’: ‘Stop Bringing Bulls–t’ Into My Shows!’ 

Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' Ties Hot Country Songs Record With 50 Weeks at No. 1 

On Sunday (Nov. 22), an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd approximately 40 minutes into the Houston-born rapper’s performance. The show was evacuated with a number of attendees receiving medical treatment and a “major incident” being declared by officials.

Following an investigation, the Greater Manchester Police has said the “release of the substance could be linked to reports of a small number of robbery offences at the arena.” They said that there were reports of nine thefts from audience members and that no arrests had been made at this time.

In their statement, local law enforcement noted they were ”aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending.”

Police are yet to identify the substance. The North West Ambulance service said 80 people were treated for “eye and respiratory symptoms,” with one person admitted to hospital. 

Writing on his Instagram Stories, Toliver said, “My heart and prayers are with with [sic] everyone that was injured last night…
items.t: ‘Unknown Substance’ Released at Evacuated Don Toliver Show in Manchester ‘Could Be Linked to Jewel Thefts,’ Police Say

items.title: Post your questions for Carl Cox
items.summary:
Ahead of him rounding out the year at a huge London show, the DJ legend will join us to answer your questions

Beatifically smiling as he sends another packed dancefloor into raptures, Carl Cox is one of the most enduring and reliably euphoria-inducing figures in UK club culture history. As he prepares to close out the current season at Drumsheds, the UK’s biggest nightclub, and looks towards a return of his residency at Ibiza nightclub Unvrs, he will join us to answer your questions.

Known for playing a banging yet nuanced blend of house and techno, Cox’s career stretches back to the age of 10, learning his craft growing up in London and later Brighton, funding nights out by trimming his neighbours’ hedges. As Chicago house, Detroit techno and other new styles hit the UK, Cox was primed to receive them: fluidly mixing across three decks at once, he immersed himself in both the illegal rave scene and the new wave of nightclubs cropping up to showcase this music.

items.title: Erykah Badu Takes Us on a Cosmic Trip For ‘Breezy’ Late-Night Performance: Watch
items.summary:
With Erykah Badu behind the wheel, what could possibly go wrong?

The five-time Grammy Award winning R&B star stopped by NBC’s The Tonight Show on Tuesday night (Nov. 24), for a performance of “Breezy,” lifted from her collaborative album with The Alchemist , Before the World Blows: The Abi and Alan Experiment .

For the musical spot, Badu drives night owls to a place they’ve never been. With a steering wheel in her hands, Badu embarks on a cosmic journey, a psychedelic trip. Once arrived at her destination, she pulls back and gets to work with her full band as “Breezy” blends into Elton John’s “Bennie and the Jets.”

Before the World Blows: The Abi and Alan Experiment is a 16-track journey into the minds of two important artists in their respective fields that came together to forge a work of art. The catalyst? More than three years ago, Badu told her longtime creative partner Cold Cris that she had always wanted to rap over Mobb Deep’s “The Realest,” a gritty Alchemist production.

Then, reps say, The Alchemist sent Badu a collection of instrumental beats, which she deconstructed and molded into tracks, before testing their creations with live audiences in 2024 and 2025, performing in intimate, phone-free spaces.

The co-produced collection dropped in August, the result of 18 months’ recording in Dallas and Los Angeles, and features contributions from DJ Creole Princess, Westside Gunn , Joi, DRAM , Steve Lacy , Thundercat , Earl Sweatshirt , Kamasi Washington , DJ Quik on percussion and Young Guru contributing to the project’s mixing efforts.

items.title: Amanda Seyfried had to get a five-factor security app just to read ‘You Can See Everything’ script
items.summary:
Amanda Seyfried has spoken about her secretive appearance in record-breaking documentary You Can See Everything .

READ MORE: ‘You Can See Everything’ review: a three-hour odyssey of deception, doubt and dodgy dealings 

Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, You Can See Everything captures Elizabeth Holmes’ final few weeks at home before the health businesswoman went to jail following her conviction for four counts of fraud for deceiving investors.

Because Fielder couldn’t record his conversations with Holmes following her imprisonment, he recruited Amanda Seyfried to recreate those encounters. Seyfried previously played Holmes in the 2022 biopic The Dropout .

Seyfried’s involvement in You Can See Everything was initially kept under wraps. But, with the documentary now available to stream in the US , she’s started doing interviews about her involvement in the project which could see her become the first documentary star to win an acting Oscar.

“At first, it was never my intention to recreate Elizabeth Holmes ever again,” Seyfried said during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon . Fielder originally reached out to “pick her brains” about her role in The Dropout after Emma Stone connected them. “We talked for an hour on Facetime, he told me he had lived with her for a month before she went to prison. I didn’t expect it.”

Fielder asked her a “bunch of questions” before offering her the chance to see the footage they’d shot for the documentary, if they could film her reaction. Eventually Seyfried started playing the part of Holmes.

items.title: AI music banned on TIDAL as they delete 29million songs
items.summary:
AI music has been banned on TIDAL, and the platform has taken down nearly 30 million songs identified as being “100 per cent AI generated recordings”.

READ MORE: What does the music industry want from the future of AI – and how can the UK lead the way? 

The change comes as the use of AI in music has become increasingly prominent in recent years, and a study conducted last year revealed that 97 per cent of people “can’t tell the difference” between real and AI music .

In June, TIDAL confirmed that it was putting a new policy in place to crack down on AI-generated music – revealing that it would no longer be paying royalties to any music made entirely by artificial intelligence.

The guidelines clarified that “artists should have the freedom to create with AI tools”, and would only be affecting music that is made entirely by “text-prompted AI”. It also said that while AI could exist on the platform, it would be offering people the option to filter it out as “listeners should have the autonomy to choose the type of content they consume”.

Now, the platform has revealed that it will be banning AI music entirely from next month.

“Since July, we’ve demonetised and labeled 100 per cent AI generated recordings. Now, we’re banning these tracks from TIDAL entirely,” a new post on TIDAL’s social media read. “If a distributor tells us a track was created solely using generative AI tools, or if we detect that it was, we’ll remove it from TIDAL.”

View this post on Instagram 

The post also shared some statistics, confirming that just 6 per cent of its “entire streaming catalogue…
items.t: AI music banned on TIDAL as they delete 29million songs

items.title: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson
items.summary:
He was the child star of the Osmonds who become a global celebrity by 14. Then, at 21, his career came crashing down. Here, he reveals how he survived his years in exile – and what happened when Jackson was accused of child abuse

For a brief period in the early 1970s, Donny Osmond ruled the world. He was the global teenage heart-throb. Even Michael Jackson trailed behind him. He was 14 when his most famous song, Puppy Love, spent five weeks at No 1 in the UK. My sister had a huge poster of him on her bedroom wall. Then again, everybody’s sister had a poster of him on their bedroom wall. Between 1972 and 1973 he had six Top 5 hits in the UK, three of them No 1s (including The Twelfth of Never and Young Love). He was equally successful back home in the US.

Osmond was clean-cut, religious and respectful, with a mighty ability to punch out cover versions of saccharine standards. From his purple velvet cap to his doleful eyes and dazzling all-American smile, he was a marketing dream. We’d only just finished with Beatlemania. And now there was Donnymania.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson

items.title: Interpol and Bloc Party review – two of 00s indie’s most revered acts go toe-to-toe
items.summary:
Utilita Arena Cardiff
Kele Okereke has a tough challenge selling Bloc Party’s trite latest album – a far cry from Interpol’s ‘masterpiece’ eighth record, performed here to darkly hypnotic effect

Try as one might to resist comparison, the balance of this particular yin and yang has been shifting for some time. Twelve months ago, when Interpol and Bloc Party announced a UK and European co-headline tour, the pairing looked like an even contest: two of 00s indie’s most revered acts, whose landmark debuts remain touchstones of the era.

Since then, their fortunes have diverged. As an opening bass drone strafes the room, Bloc Party arrive in Cardiff in superficially fine, if puzzling, form. Their seventh album, Anatomy of a Brief Romance, has been met with diminishing returns, its Snapchat-caption triteness – “Every day is such a vibe”, runs one refrain – and creative inertia doing little to win over listeners.

items.title: Fontaines DC review – thrilling gothic grandeur from a band vaulting into greatness
items.summary:
M&S Bank Arena, Liverpool
Just a few years since playing little dive bars, the Irish rockers have confidently scaled up to huge rooms like this – and are now one of the key interpreters of modern malaise

A mere seven years since their debut, Dogrel, Fontaines DC have enjoyed a virtually seamless passage from Dublin dive bars to arenas, with stadiums to follow next year. Each step has been taken seemingly effortlessly in their stride and this latest outing is no exception. Bathed in shimmering blue light, the band are well into hymnal opener Six Shot Morning before we even see sight of singer Grian Chatten. He wanders on while singing, an entrance worthy of Frank Sinatra.

Chatten has previously seemed to distrust showbiz, but if anything the singer seems far more comfortable on the bigger stage than he ever did on smaller ones. With his Korn T-shirt, unfeasibly baggy trousers and tiny tattoo reading “deadly” in capitals, he leaps around, raises his arms to whip up the crowd and points the microphone towards them to sing key lines. Similarly, music this intense, dark, elegiac and even bleak – which speaks to the void at the heart of much modern life – is hardly typical arena fare but works brilliantly by taking on a more anthemic, celebratory aspect. It’s certainly weirdly thrilling hearing Chatten’s lines such as “We’re all depressed, running on a wheel” or “I don’t feel anything in the modern world” – or a song as plainly dark as Jackie Down the Line – become enormous, arena-uniting sing-songs.
items.t: Fontaines DC review – thrilling gothic grandeur from a band vaulting into greatness
